classes.name: A journey test failed after merge and the change's own test run did not catch it
classes.description: An end-to-end journey (a scripted run of a whole user path) fails on main, or in a batch or gate run, after the change landed. The change's own journey run left that journey out, or did not exercise what the change touched. Timing races that make a journey fail after merge belong here too.

classes.name: A document, comment or report said something the code or data does not back
classes.description: A wrong fact, a wrong line citation, a summary that claims more than was done, or a doc that contradicts the code it describes.

classes.name: The change does not do what the approved request promised
classes.description: A requirement or deliverable is missing, a design contradicts the approved intent, or a step cannot be run as written.

classes.name: An error, retry, rollback or odd-input case was not handled
classes.description: The normal path works, but a failure, a partial state, an unusual input, a repeat run or an undo leaves things wrong or crashes.

classes.name: Plain wrong logic or state on the normal path
classes.description: A wrong condition, count, order or comparison; stale or double-counted data; the code does something other than what its author meant.

classes.name: A test or proof does not check what it claims
classes.description: A test that cannot fail, depends on timing, skips its control run, is not run, or hand-copies the thing it should test.

classes.name: A repo or process rule was skipped
classes.description: A required route, document, decision record, review step or repo convention was not followed.

classes.name: It behaves differently in the real environment
classes.description: Platform, deploy settings, permissions, size limits or load make the real run differ from the author's run.
